chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said:

“The one who eats carrion, blood, and the flesh of swine—upon them is disciplinary punishment; and if he repeats it, he is disciplined.” I said: “Then if he repeats, is he to be disciplined?” He said: “He is to be disciplined, and there is no fixed hadd punishment upon him.”

key_terms.أَدَبٌ: disciplinary punishment or chastisement imposed by authority
key_terms.الدَّمِ: blood as a prohibited substance for consumption
key_terms.الْمَيْتَةِ: carrion, an animal found dead without lawful slaughter
key_terms.حَدٌّ: a fixed prescribed punishment in sacred law
key_terms.لَحْمِ الْخِنْزِيرِ: the flesh of swine, which is forbidden to eat

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on repeatedly eating carrion, blood, or pork in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that one who consumes prohibited foods such as carrion, blood, and pork is subject to disciplinary punishment. If the act is repeated, the person is again disciplined, but no fixed hadd punishment applies in this case.
